claim: Exosomes are small vesicles that are secreted from metazoan cells.
source: Exosomes are small vesicles that are secreted from metazoan cells and may convey selected membrane proteins and small RNAs to target cells for the control of cell migration, development and metastasis.
evidence: This is a statement from the abstract describing the nature of exosomes, drawing on established scientific knowledge.

claim: Exosomes may convey selected membrane proteins and small RNAs to target cells for the control of cell migration, development and metastasis.
source: Exosomes are small vesicles that are secreted from metazoan cells and may convey selected membrane proteins and small RNAs to target cells for the control of cell migration, development and metastasis.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential function of exosomes.

claim: A purification scheme based on the membrane marker CD63 was devised to isolate a single exosome species secreted from HEK293T cells.
source: To study the mechanisms of RNA packaging into exosomes, we devised a purification scheme based on the membrane marker CD63 to isolate a single exosome species secreted from HEK293T cells.
evidence: This describes a methodological approach developed in the study.

claim: A set of miRNAs are highly enriched in CD63-containing exosomes with respect to their cellular levels.
source: Using immunoisolated CD63-containing exosomes we identified a set of miRNAs that are highly enriched with respect to their cellular levels.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on experimental data.

claim: A cell-free reaction was devised that recapitulates the species-selective enclosure of miR-223 in isolated membranes supplemented with cytosol.
source: To explore the biochemical requirements for exosome biogenesis and RNA packaging, we devised a cell-free reaction that recapitulates the species-selective enclosure of miR-223 in isolated membranes supplemented with cytosol.
evidence: This describes a methodological development and its outcome.

claim: YBX1 binds to miR-223.
source: We found that the RNA-binding protein Y-box protein I (YBX1) binds to and is required for the sorting of miR-223 in the cell-free reaction.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on experimental data.

claim: YBX1 is required for the sorting of miR-223 in the cell-free reaction.
source: We found that the RNA-binding protein Y-box protein I (YBX1) binds to and is required for the sorting of miR-223 in the cell-free reaction.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on experimental data.

claim: YBX1 serves an important role in the secretion of miRNAs in exosomes by HEK293T cells.
source: Furthermore, YBX1 serves an important role in the secretion of miRNAs in exosomes by HEK293T cells.
evidence: This is a finding from the study based on experimental data.

claim: Unconventionally secreted molecules may be externalized in a soluble form by translocation across various membranes.
source: Unconventionally secreted molecules may be externalized in a soluble form by translocation across various membranes.
evidence: This is a statement about known mechanisms of unconventional secretion.

claim: Proteins and RNAs can be secreted within vesicles that bud from the plasma membrane.
source: Alternatively, proteins and RNAs can be secreted within vesicles that bud from the plasma membrane, as in the budding of enveloped viruses such as HIV, or within vesicles internalized into a multivesicular body (MVB) that fuses with the plasma membrane (Colombo et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement about known mechanisms of secretion, supported by citation.

claim: RNA is actively secreted into the medium of cultured cells.
source: RNA is actively secreted into the medium of cultured cells and can be found in all bodily fluids enclosed within vesicles or bound up in ribonucleoprotin complexes, both forms of which are resistant to exogenous ribonuclease (Colombo et al., 2014; Arroyo et al., 2011; Mitchell et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a statement about known phenomena, supported by citations.

claim: RNA can be found in all bodily fluids enclosed within vesicles or bound up in ribonucleoprotin complexes.
source: RNA is actively secreted into the medium of cultured cells and can be found in all bodily fluids enclosed within vesicles or bound up in ribonucleoprotin complexes, both forms of which are resistant to exogenous ribonuclease (Colombo et al., 2014; Arroyo et al., 2011; Mitchell et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a statement about known phenomena, supported by citations.

claim: Extracellular vesicle-bound RNAs and ribonucleoprotein complexes are resistant to exogenous ribonuclease.
source: RNA is actively secreted into the medium of cultured cells and can be found in all bodily fluids enclosed within vesicles or bound up in ribonucleoprotin complexes, both forms of which are resistant to exogenous ribonuclease (Colombo et al., 2014; Arroyo et al., 2011; Mitchell et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a statement about known phenomena, supported by citations.

claim: Extracellular vesicle-bound RNAs appear to be enriched in specific classes of RNAs, including small RNAs and microRNA (miRNA).
source: Importantly, extracellular vesicle-bound RNAs appear to be enriched in specific classes of RNAs, including small RNAs and microRNA (miRNA) (Skog et al., 2008; Valadi et al., 2007; Kosaka et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a statement about known phenomena, supported by citations.

claim: Exosomes are a subclass of extracellular vesicle which can be defined as 30–100 nm vesicles with a buoyant density of ~1.10–1.19 g/ml that are enriched in specific biochemical markers, including tetraspanin proteins.
source: Exosomes are a subclass of extracellular vesicle which can be defined as 30–100 nm vesicles with a buoyant density of ~1.10–1.19 g/ml that are enriched in specific biochemical markers, including tetraspanin proteins (Colombo et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a definition based on established knowledge and citation.

claim: It is often assumed that vesicles fitting the exosome description are derived from the multivesicular body.
source: It is often assumed that vesicles fitting this description are derived from the multivesicular body, but some evidence suggests that physically and biochemically indistinguishable vesicles bud directly from the plasma membrane (Booth et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a statement about common assumptions in the field, supported by citation.

claim: Some evidence suggests that physically and biochemically indistinguishable vesicles bud directly from the plasma membrane.
source: It is often assumed that vesicles fitting this description are derived from the multivesicular body, but some evidence suggests that physically and biochemically indistinguishable vesicles bud directly from the plasma membrane (Booth et al., 2006).
evidence: This is a statement about alternative hypotheses, supported by citation.

claim: Many studies have relied on isolation techniques that do not resolve vesicles from other cellular debris or RNPs.
source: Numerous studies have reported the presence of RNAs, especially miRNAs, from fractions containing exosomes, though many of these studies have relied on isolation techniques (e.g. high speed sedimentation) that do not resolve vesicles from other cellular debris or RNPs (Bobrie et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a critical assessment of previous studies, supported by citation.

claim: It is difficult to know in which form RNAs are secreted.
source: Thus, it is difficult to know in which form RNAs are secreted and even more challenging to determine which miRNAs may be specifically secreted as exosome cargo.
evidence: This is an inference based on the limitations of previous studies.

claim: RNA profiles from exosomes are distinct from those of the producer cells.
source: Even with the crude preparations that have been characterized, it is clear that RNA profiles from exosomes are distinct from those of the producer cells.
evidence: This is a statement about known phenomena based on previous studies.

claim: RNA capture or stabilization in exosomes is likely to occur through a selective sorting mechanism.
source: Thus RNA capture or stabilization in exosomes is likely to occur through a selective sorting mechanism.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that RNA profiles differ between exosomes and cells.

claim: RNA packaging may occur by specific interactions with RNA binding proteins that engage the machinery necessary for membrane invagination into the interior of an MVB.
source: RNA packaging may occur by specific interactions with RNA binding proteins that engage the machinery necessary for membrane invagination into the interior of an MVB or by interaction of RNAs with lipid raft microdomains from which exosomes may be derived (Janas et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about possible mechanisms, supported by citation.

claim: RNA packaging may occur by interaction of RNAs with lipid raft microdomains from which exosomes may be derived.
source: RNA packaging may occur by specific interactions with RNA binding proteins that engage the machinery necessary for membrane invagination into the interior of an MVB or by interaction of RNAs with lipid raft microdomains from which exosomes may be derived (Janas et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about possible mechanisms, supported by citation.

claim: Purified exosomes were recovered using a three-stage purification procedure.
source: Based on these criteria, purified exosomes were recovered using a three-stage purification procedure (Figure 1a).
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study, with reference to a figure.

claim: Analysis of partially purified material by electron microscopy showed vesicles of the expected size and morphology with fewer profiles of larger (>200 nm) membranes and reduced appearance of protein aggregates.
source: Analysis of this partially purified material by electron microscopy showed vesicles of the expected size and morphology with fewer profiles of larger (>200 nm) membranes and reduced appearance of protein aggregates (Figure 1b,c compared to Figure 1d,e).
evidence: This is a finding from electron microscopy analysis, with reference to figures.

claim: CD63-luciferase activity was stimulated by the addition of detergent to disrupt the membrane.
source: Luciferase activity was stimulated by the addition of detergent to disrupt the membrane and allow access to the membrane impermeable substrates luciferin and ATP, and to trypsin, which inactivated luciferase activity in the presence but not in the absence of detergent (Figure 1f).
evidence: This is a finding from the luciferase activity assay, with reference to a figure.

claim: Trypsin inactivated luciferase activity in the presence but not in the absence of detergent.
source: Luciferase activity was stimulated by the addition of detergent to disrupt the membrane and allow access to the membrane impermeable substrates luciferin and ATP, and to trypsin, which inactivated luciferase activity in the presence but not in the absence of detergent (Figure 1f).
evidence: This is a finding from the luciferase activity assay, with reference to a figure.

claim: CD63-luciferase specific activity increased at each step of the purification, yielding a 5-fold purification of exosomes from the starting 100,000 ×g pellet.
source: CD63-luciferase specific activity increased at each step of the purification, yielding a 5-fold purification of exosomes from the starting 100,000 ×g pellet (Figure 1g).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the purification process, with reference to a figure.

claim: Following immunoisolation, most of the RNA was found in the CD63 positive bound (B) fraction.
source: Additionally, following immunoisolation, most of the RNA was found in the CD63 positive bound (B) fraction, showing that RNA is associated with purified exosomes from HEK293T cells (Figure 1f).
evidence: This is a finding from the immunoisolation experiment, with reference to a figure.

claim: RNA is associated with purified exosomes from HEK293T cells.
source: Additionally, following immunoisolation, most of the RNA was found in the CD63 positive bound (B) fraction, showing that RNA is associated with purified exosomes from HEK293T cells (Figure 1f).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the immunoisolation data, with reference to a figure.

claim: A total of 123,679 miRNA reads (4.4% of total mapped reads) were obtained in the exosome library representing 502 distinct miRNAs.
source: We obtained a total of 123,679 miRNA reads (4.4% of total mapped reads – Figure 2—source data 1) in the exosome library representing 502 distinct miRNAs and 880,093 reads (7.3% of total mapped reads – Figure 2—source data 1) representing 637 miRNAs in the cell library (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from small RNA sequencing, with reference to a figure and source data.

claim: A total of 880,093 reads (7.3% of total mapped reads) representing 637 miRNAs were obtained in the cell library.
source: We obtained a total of 123,679 miRNA reads (4.4% of total mapped reads – Figure 2—source data 1) in the exosome library representing 502 distinct miRNAs and 880,093 reads (7.3% of total mapped reads – Figure 2—source data 1) representing 637 miRNAs in the cell library (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from small RNA sequencing, with reference to a figure and source data.

claim: Exosomes were slightly enriched in reads mapping to precursor and passenger strand transcripts.
source: Exosomes were slightly enriched in reads mapping to precursor and passenger strand transcripts, however, the vast majority of miRNAs (91% from cells and 88% from exosomes) mapped to the mature targeting strand.
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of small RNA sequencing data.

claim: The vast majority of miRNAs (91% from cells and 88% from exosomes) mapped to the mature targeting strand.
source: Exosomes were slightly enriched in reads mapping to precursor and passenger strand transcripts, however, the vast majority of miRNAs (91% from cells and 88% from exosomes) mapped to the mature targeting strand.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the analysis of small RNA sequencing data.

claim: 134 miRNAs were uniquely found in the exosome dataset.
source: Of these, 134 and 269 miRNAs were uniquely found in the exosome and cell datasets respectively (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the comparison of exosome and cell miRNA datasets, with reference to a figure.

claim: 269 miRNAs were uniquely found in the cell dataset.
source: Of these, 134 and 269 miRNAs were uniquely found in the exosome and cell datasets respectively (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the comparison of exosome and cell miRNA datasets, with reference to a figure.

claim: Most of the miRNAs uniquely found in exosomes were of very low abundance.
source: Most of the miRNAs uniquely found in exosomes were of very low abundance, with only a few counts for each miRNA.
evidence: This is a qualitative observation from the analysis of exosome-specific miRNAs.

claim: miR-223-3p was in the 72nd percentile for normalized reads in exosomes.
source: A notable exception was miR-223-3p, which was in the 72nd percentile for normalized reads in exosomes (Figure 2c,d – red).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding about miR-223-3p abundance in exosomes, with reference to a figure.

claim: The relatively high abundance of miR-223 in exosomes and its low level in the cellular library indicated that miR-223 was very efficiently packaged and secreted via exosomes.
source: The relatively high abundance of miR-223 in exosomes and its low level in the cellular library indicated that miR-223 was very efficiently packaged and secreted via exosomes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the relative abundance of miR-223 in exosomes versus cells.

claim: A total of 368 miRNAs were detected in both the exosome and cell libraries.
source: A total of 368 miRNAs were detected in both the exosome and cell libraries.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the comparison of exosome and cell miRNA datasets.

claim: Some miRNAs (e.g. miR144-3p, miR150-5p, miR142-3p) were highly enriched in exosomes and moderately abundant in exosomes.
source: Most of these miRNAs were more enriched in cells than exosomes; however, some (e.g. miR144-3p, miR150-5p, miR142-3p) were highly enriched in exosomes and, like miR223, were moderately abundant in exosomes (Figure 2c,d - yellow).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis of miRNA enrichment in exosomes, with reference to a figure.

claim: qRT-PCR results showed a selective enrichment of both miR-223 and miR-144 at each stage of the purification.
source: We performed quantitative reverse transcriptase PCR (qRT-PCR) for each miRNA target during the course of exosome purification from conditioned medium. Our results showed a selective enrichment of both miR-223 and miR-144 at each stage of the purification (Figure 2e and f).
evidence: This is a finding from qRT-PCR analysis, with reference to figures.

claim: miR-223 and miR-144 are associated with CD63 exosomes.
source: Thus, these miRNAs are associated with CD63 exosomes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the enrichment data.

claim: Both miR-223 and miR-144 were protected from RNase I digestion, unless detergent was added to disrupt the membrane.
source: Both miRNAs were protected from RNase I digestion, unless detergent was added to disrupt the membrane (Figure 2g).
evidence: This is a finding from the RNase protection assay, with reference to a figure.

claim: miRNAs are selectively packaged into exosomes purified from HEK293T conditioned media.
source: These results confirm that miRNAs are selectively packaged into exosomes purified from HEK293T conditioned media and establish miR-223 and miR-144 as specific exosomal miRNAs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the RNase protection and enrichment data.

claim: miR-223 and miR-144 are specific exosomal miRNAs.
source: These results confirm that miRNAs are selectively packaged into exosomes purified from HEK293T conditioned media and establish miR-223 and miR-144 as specific exosomal miRNAs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the RNase protection and enrichment data.

claim: The formation of sequestered luciferase required cytosol and incubation at 30°C and was disrupted in incubations containing detergent (Triton X-100).
source: We observed that the formation of sequestered luciferase required cytosol and incubation at 30°C and was disrupted in incubations containing detergent (Triton X-100) (Figure 3b).
evidence: This is a finding from the cell-free exosome biogenesis assay, with reference to a figure.

claim: The cell-free reaction conditions reconstitute the formation of exosomes.
source: These results suggest that our conditions reconstitute the formation of exosomes in a cell-free reaction.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the cell-free biogenesis assay data.

claim: Packaging of miR-223 required membranes, cytosol and incubation at physiologic temperature.
source: Packaging of miR-223 required membranes, cytosol and incubation at physiologic temperature (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is a finding from the cell-free miRNA packaging assay, with reference to a figure.

claim: Addition of TX-100 during the RNase incubation abrogated protection of miR-223.
source: As expected for the segregation of miR-223 into a membrane bound compartment, addition of TX-100 during the RNase incubation abrogated protection (Figure 4b).
evidence: This is a finding from the cell-free miRNA packaging assay, with reference to a figure.

claim: At a minimal concentration of cytosol (0.5 mg/ml), protection was stimulated two-fold over reactions performed in the absence of ATP, or in the presence of apyrase or a non-hydrolyzable analog of ATP.
source: Furthermore, at a minimal concentration of cytosol (0.5 mg/ml), protection was stimulated two-fold over reactions performed in the in the absence of ATP, or in the presence of apyrase or a non-hydrolyzable analog of ATP (Figure 4c).
evidence: This is a finding from the cell-free miRNA packaging assay, with reference to a figure.

claim: GW4869 inhibited the protection of CD63-luciferase and miR-223 in cell-free assays at concentrations required to inhibit NS2 activity in partially purified fractions of the enzyme.
source: GW4869 inhibited the protection of CD63-luciferase and miR-223 in our cell-free assays at concentrations required to inhibit NS2 activity in partially purified fractions of the enzyme (Figure 4d) (Luberto et al., 2002).
evidence: This is a finding from the cell-free assays with inhibitor treatment, with reference to a figure and citation.

claim: The cell-free reactions may recapitulate an aspect of exosome biogenesis.
source: Thus, our cell-free reactions may recapitulate an aspect of exosome biogenesis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the inhibitor experiment data.

claim: Exosomal miR-223 was more efficiently packaged into vesicles (9%) than cellular miR-190 (1.5%).
source: Exosomal miR-223 was more efficiently packaged into vesicles (9%) than cellular miR-190 (1.5%) (Figure 4e).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the cell-free packaging assay comparing two miRNAs, with reference to a figure.

claim: The rate of miR-223 packaging mirrored the rate at which luciferase became sequestered in the biogenesis reaction.
source: Furthermore, the rate of miR-223 packaging mirrored the rate at which luciferase became sequestered in the biogenesis reaction whereas the rate of miR-190 protection in a 30°C incubation reflected the low rate of formation of sequestered luciferase in an incubation held on ice (Figure 4f).
evidence: This is a finding from the time-course analysis of the cell-free assays, with reference to a figure.

claim: The cell-free packaging assay reconstitutes the selective sorting of exosomal miR-223 over cellular miR-190 into vesicles, possibly exosomes, formed in vitro.
source: Based on these experiments, we conclude that the cell-free packaging assay reconstitutes the selective sorting of exosomal miR-223 over cellular miR-190 into vesicles, possibly exosomes, formed in vitro.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the selective packaging data.

claim: The most highly represented protein identified by mass spectrometry was Y-box binding protein I (YBX1).
source: Based on peptide count and coverage, the most highly represented protein was Y-box binding protein I (YBX1) (Figure 5b).
evidence: This is a finding from the mass spectrometry analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: Peptides representing >45% YBX1 of the protein were identified stretching from the cold shock domain to the C-terminus.
source: Peptides representing >45% YBX1 of the protein were identified stretching from the cold shock domain to the C-terminus (Figure 5c).
evidence: This is a finding from the mass spectrometry analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: YBX1 is a multi-functional RNA binding protein that shuttles between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.
source: YBX1 is a multi-functional RNA binding protein that shuttles between the nucleus, where it plays a role and splice site selection (Wang et al., 2013; Wei et al., 2012), and the cytoplasm where it is required for the recruitment of RNAs into cytoplasmic ribonucleoprotein granules containing untranslated mRNAs and plays a role in mRNA stability (Lyabin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement about known functions of YBX1, supported by citations.

claim: YBX1 plays a role in splice site selection in the nucleus.
source: YBX1 is a multi-functional RNA binding protein that shuttles between the nucleus, where it plays a role and splice site selection (Wang et al., 2013; Wei et al., 2012), and the cytoplasm where it is required for the recruitment of RNAs into cytoplasmic ribonucleoprotein granules containing untranslated mRNAs and plays a role in mRNA stability (Lyabin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement about known functions of YBX1, supported by citations.

claim: YBX1 is required for the recruitment of RNAs into cytoplasmic ribonucleoprotein granules containing untranslated mRNAs in the cytoplasm.
source: YBX1 is a multi-functional RNA binding protein that shuttles between the nucleus, where it plays a role and splice site selection (Wang et al., 2013; Wei et al., 2012), and the cytoplasm where it is required for the recruitment of RNAs into cytoplasmic ribonucleoprotein granules containing untranslated mRNAs and plays a role in mRNA stability (Lyabin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement about known functions of YBX1, supported by citations.

claim: YBX1 plays a role in mRNA stability in the cytoplasm.
source: YBX1 is a multi-functional RNA binding protein that shuttles between the nucleus, where it plays a role and splice site selection (Wang et al., 2013; Wei et al., 2012), and the cytoplasm where it is required for the recruitment of RNAs into cytoplasmic ribonucleoprotein granules containing untranslated mRNAs and plays a role in mRNA stability (Lyabin et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement about known functions of YBX1, supported by citations.

claim: YBX1 co-localizes with cytoplasmic P-bodies containing members of the RISC complex, including GW182.
source: YBX1 also co-localizes with cytoplasmic P-bodies containing members of the RISC complex, including GW182 which can be found in exosomes (Goodier et al., 2007; Gallois-Montbrun et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a statement about known localization of YBX1, supported by citations.

claim: GW182 can be found in exosomes.
source: YBX1 also co-localizes with cytoplasmic P-bodies containing members of the RISC complex, including GW182 which can be found in exosomes (Goodier et al., 2007; Gallois-Montbrun et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a statement about known localization of GW182, supported by citations.

claim: YBX1 is secreted in a form that resists trypsin in the absence but not in the presence of a non-ionic detergent (Triton X-100).
source: Interestingly, YBX1 is secreted in a form that resists trypsin in the absence but not in the presence of a non-ionic detergent (Triton X-100), consistent with a location in vesicles, perhaps exosomes (Frye et al., 2009; Rauen et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a statement about known properties of secreted YBX1, supported by citations.

claim: YBX1 has been detected by mass spectrometry in isolated exosomes.
source: Furthermore, YBX1 has been detected by mass spectrometry in isolated exosomes (Ung et al., 2014; Buschow et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a statement about previous findings, supported by citations.

claim: YBX1 was primarily associated with the CD63-bound fraction containing known exosome markers (TSG101, Alix, CD9).
source: We purified exosomes as in Figure 1a and found that YBX1 was primarily associated with the CD63-bound fraction containing known exosome markers (TSG101, Alix, CD9), as opposed to flotillin 2, which was predominantly found in the unbound fraction (Figure 5d).
evidence: This is a finding from the exosome purification and immunoblot analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: Flotillin 2 was predominantly found in the unbound fraction.
source: We purified exosomes as in Figure 1a and found that YBX1 was primarily associated with the CD63-bound fraction containing known exosome markers (TSG101, Alix, CD9), as opposed to flotillin 2, which was predominantly found in the unbound fraction (Figure 5d).
evidence: This is a finding from the exosome purification and immunoblot analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: The CD63 positive (exosome) fraction contained most of the RNA.
source: The CD63 positive (exosome) fraction contained most of the RNA (Figure 1f).
evidence: This is a finding from the exosome purification, with reference to a figure.

claim: HEK293T cells release at least two vesicle types (CD63 positive and negative).
source: These results show that HEK293T cells release at least two vesicle types (CD63 positive and negative).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the differential distribution of markers.

claim: YBX1 bound to biotin-miR-223 was recovered in exosomes in a complete reaction.
source: An immunoblot showed YBX1 bound to biotin-mi223 was recovered in exosomes in a complete reaction, while no detectable YBX1 was recovered in exosomes in incubations that lacked cytosol or membranes and much reduced signals in control incubations held at 4C or conducted in the absence of biotin-mi223 (Figure 5e).
evidence: This is a finding from the biotin-miR-223 pull-down assay, with reference to a figure.

claim: No detectable YBX1 was recovered in exosomes in incubations that lacked cytosol or membranes.
source: An immunoblot showed YBX1 bound to biotin-mi223 was recovered in exosomes in a complete reaction, while no detectable YBX1 was recovered in exosomes in incubations that lacked cytosol or membranes and much reduced signals in control incubations held at 4C or conducted in the absence of biotin-mi223 (Figure 5e).
evidence: This is a finding from the biotin-miR-223 pull-down assay, with reference to a figure.

claim: Much reduced YBX1 signals were observed in control incubations held at 4°C or conducted in the absence of biotin-miR-223.
source: An immunoblot showed YBX1 bound to biotin-mi223 was recovered in exosomes in a complete reaction, while no detectable YBX1 was recovered in exosomes in incubations that lacked cytosol or membranes and much reduced signals in control incubations held at 4C or conducted in the absence of biotin-mi223 (Figure 5e).
evidence: This is a finding from the biotin-miR-223 pull-down assay, with reference to a figure.

claim: The conditions for YBX1 co-packaging with miR-223 mirror those required for the packaging of miR-223 in the cell-free reaction.
source: These conditions mirror those required for the packaging of miR-223 in our cell-free reaction.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing the requirements for YBX1 binding and miR-223 packaging.

claim: Argonaute proteins have been variously described as being inside of extracellular vesicles or released as free proteins independent of vesicles.
source: Argonaute proteins have been variously described as being inside of extracellular vesicles (Arroyo et al., 2011; Turchinovich et al., 2011) or released as free proteins independent of vesicles (Squadrito et al., 2014; Gibbings et al., 2009).
evidence: This is a statement about conflicting reports in the literature, supported by citations.

claim: After flotation, the exosome marker proteins were enriched compared to the pellet fraction.
source: As expected, after flotation the exosome marker proteins were enriched compared to the pellet fraction (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is a finding from the flotation and immunoblot analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: Ago2 was not detected in the density gradient purified vesicle fraction.
source: In contrast, Ago2 was not detected in the density gradient purified vesicle fraction (Figure 6a).
evidence: This is a finding from the flotation and immunoblot analysis, with reference to a figure.

claim: In HEK293T cells the large majority of extracellular Ago2 exists as a non-vesicle associated species.
source: Regardless, our results show that in HEK293T cells the large majority of extracellular Ago2 exists as a non-vesicle associated species.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the failure to detect Ago2 in purified vesicles.

claim: Ago2 is not associated with density gradient purified exosomes isolated from breast cancer (MCF7) cells.
source: These results support previously published evidence that Ago is not associated with density gradient purified exosomes isolated from breast cancer (MCF7) cells (Van Deun et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement about supporting evidence from another study, with citation.

claim: Both the single stranded guide and duplex oligonucleotides bound apparently equally to Ago2 in cytosol alone.
source: In our reaction conditions, both the single stranded guide and duplex oligonucleotides bound apparently equally to Ago2 in cytosol alone and there was no discernible difference in the association comparing 3' or internally biotinylated oligonucleotides (Figure 6c).
evidence: This is a finding from the Ago2 binding assay, with reference to a figure.

claim: There was no discernible difference in Ago2 association comparing 3' or internally biotinylated oligonucleotides.
source: In our reaction conditions, both the single stranded guide and duplex oligonucleotides bound apparently equally to Ago2 in cytosol alone and there was no discernible difference in the association comparing 3' or internally biotinylated oligonucleotides (Figure 6c).
evidence: This is a finding from the Ago2 binding assay, with reference to a figure.

claim: Duplex substrates were packaged ~2-fold more efficiently than the single stranded guide RNA, irrespective of the position of the biotin group.
source: Duplex substrates were packaged ~2-fold more efficiently than the single stranded guide RNA, irrespective of the position of the biotin group (Figure 6d).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the packaging assay, with reference to a figure.

claim: In reactions programmed with duplex RNA substrate, only the guide RNA and not the passenger RNA was sorted into a protected compartment.
source: Interestingly, in reactions programmed with duplex RNA substrate, only the guide RNA and not the passenger RNA was sorted into a protected compartment (Figure 6d).
evidence: This is a finding from the packaging assay with duplex substrates, with reference to a figure.

claim: YBX1 protein was ~2X more efficiently packaged in reactions programmed with duplex RNA.
source: In similar incubations, the YBX1 protein was ~2X more efficiently packaged in reactions programmed with duplex RNA but Ago2 was not detected associated with miR-223 in any of the complete reactions (Figure 6e,f).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the packaging assay, with reference to figures.

claim: Ago2 was not detected associated with miR-223 in any of the complete reactions.
source: In similar incubations, the YBX1 protein was ~2X more efficiently packaged in reactions programmed with duplex RNA but Ago2 was not detected associated with miR-223 in any of the complete reactions (Figure 6e,f).
evidence: This is a finding from the packaging assay, with reference to figures.

claim: Whereas the RNA substrates are capable of being bound by Ago2 in the cytosol, in the complete reaction containing membranes and ATP, YBX1 is the predominant binding factor.
source: This suggests that whereas the RNA substrates are capable of being bound by Ago2 in the cytosol, in the complete reaction containing membranes and ATP, YBX1 is the predominant binding factor.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the differential binding of Ago2 and YBX1 under different conditions.

claim: Van Deun et al. (2014) found no evidence of Ago2 in density gradient-isolated exosomes from MCF7 cells.
source: Similarly, Van Deun et al. (2014) found no evidence of Ago2 in density gradient-isolated exosomes from MCF7 cells (Van Deun et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a statement about findings from another study, with citation.

claim: A homozygous mutant clone (ΔYBX1) was recovered that had been targeted at the YBX1 locus and no longer expressed YBX1 protein.
source: We recovered a homozygous mutant clone (ΔYBX1) that had been targeted at the YBX1 locus and no longer expressed YBX1 protein (Figure 7a).

claim: The homozygous mutant ΔYBX1 cells grew normally under the conditions used to propagate HEK293T cells.
